Shakti Rathore @ Vishwas
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Prakhar Naveriya - Advocate for the applicant.

Ms. Ranjana Agnihotri - Deputy Government Advocate fo
 respondent/State.

Order 
This is repeat (second) application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS/ 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.662/23 registered at Police Station - Habibganj, District Bhopal (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366,
376(2)(N) of the IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in detention since 05.02.2024.

Applicant's first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn on 10.09.2025.
2.
As per prosecution story, allegation against the present applicant is that he committed an offence against the minor prosecutrix, therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against him.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
He is under custody NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:24907 2 MCRC-4131-2026 since 05.02.2024.
It is submitted that age of prosecutrix is 17 years 8 months.
It is further submitted that the prosecutrix herself went with the applicant and married with applicant.
She is a consenting party.
Photographs have been annexed.
Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
4. Learned Government Advocate for the State on the other hand has opposed the application and submitted prosecutrix has deposed against the present applicant.
Applicant has committed rape with minor prosecutrix.
DNA report is positive.
It is further submitted that applicant is having criminal record of nine cases in which one case is of the same nature under POCSO Act.
Hence, he prayed for dismissal of this bail application.

sentences.text: 5. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary.

6. Having taken into consideration overall facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the seriousness of offence, I am of the view that it is not a fit case in which the applicant may be released on bail.
7. Consequently, this second bail application under Section 483 of BNSS/439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands dismissed.
8. Status report has been received from the trial Court.
As per the status report, 17 witnesses have been examined and 10 witnesses are yet to be examined.

9. Looking to the aforesaid, learned trial Court is directed to conclude the trial expeditiously preferably within a period of six months from the date NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:24907 3 MCRC-4131-2026 of receipt of copy of this order.
10. It is also found that the prosecution witnesses are not appearing before the trial Court

, therefore,
the Commissioner of Police, Bhopal is directed to ensure the presence of the prosecution witnesses before the trial Court and the trial Court is also directed to take steps for the presence of other prosecution witnesses.
11.
Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the concerned trial Court as well as the Commissioner of Police, Bhopal for necessary compliance.
(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE vai Shakti Rathore @ Vishwas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 March, 2026
